origin.summary: Deniz grew up in Meridian Harbor apprenticing under a demanding mapmaker, driven to prove that patient observation can reveal what official charts miss.

origin_facts.fact: Deniz is formally bonded as an apprentice cartographer to a respected but exacting mapmaker.
Deniz's father, a surveyor, left on a charting voyage toward the Outer Mist Line and never returned.
Harbor crews treat Deniz as a serious junior professional, not a passenger.

formative_events.summary: Deniz's father vanished on an expedition years ago, and his final survey notes were never officially validated.
formative_events.impact: Instilled Deniz's obsession with evidence that cannot be dismissed or lost.

formative_events.summary: Deniz once caught a genuine error in a published inner-strait chart.
formative_events.impact: Earned grudging respect from the mapmaker and cemented Deniz's identity as an observer.

origin_relationships.subject: a close friend who prefers experiments to theories
a demanding mapmaker
origin_relationships.historical_role: trains and evaluates Deniz's work strictly on evidence
origin_relationships.unresolved_tension: Deniz suspects the mentor sometimes withholds records without explanation.

origin_relationships.subject: Deniz's missing father
origin_relationships.historical_role: surveyor lost on an outer expedition
origin_relationships.unresolved_tension: Whether his final notes hold truth no one has verified.

unresolved_origin_questions.question: What actually happened to Deniz's father on his last voyage?
Does the mentor know more about the father's last report than admitted?

present_situation.summary: Deniz is a trusted apprentice noticing that several beacon readings and old charts contradict each other in ways too consistent to be simple error.
present_situation.current_role: apprentice cartographer under supervised but increasingly independent fieldwork
present_situation.current_location_context: based in Meridian Harbor, with growing access to Beacon Ridge and nearby mapped islands
current_relationship_context: practical-minded close friend willing to help test theories
demanding mapmaker who grades evidence harshly
harbor crews who trust Deniz's competence
current_resources: a small circle of people willing to vouch for Deniz
current_pressures: several beacons disagree with official charts
outer routes are becoming commercially urgent
storm season will soon limit expeditions
current_open_questions: Why do some navigation markers not match any known chart-making era?
Are the beacon discrepancies natural drift or something else?
immediate_desires: earn the right to chart beyond the home strait
find hard evidence others cannot dismiss
immediate_avoidances: being dismissed as a reckless or overconfident child surveyor

identity_anchors.statement: Deniz believes careful observation matters more than authority or bravado.
Deniz wants recognition earned through proof, not granted by rank.

core_drives.drive: Prove that rigorous observation reveals truths official maps miss.
Earn the right to chart beyond the home strait.

core_fears.fear: Being seen as too young or too eager to be trusted with real evidence.
Being confidently wrong and damaging trust built through careful work.

internal_tensions.side_b: pull toward reckless pursuit of a personally meaningful mystery
internal_tensions.description: Deniz's discipline is tested whenever a discovery brushes close to personal stakes.

long_term_questions.question: Why do certain ancient navigation markers no longer match any official chart?

themes: the sea as an unfinished map

main_saga.title: The Uncharted Disagreement
main_saga.goal: Discover why the Shattered Meridian's ancient navigation infrastructure and living tides no longer agree with official charts.
main_saga.stakes: Outer routes vital to island trade may become unsafe or unusable if the true cause of the discrepancies goes unaddressed.
main_saga.central_mystery: Something in the deep channels or the ancient beacon-markers is behaving in ways no known chart-making era can explain.

anchors.title: Noticing the Drift
anchors.purpose: Establish Deniz's first credible pattern of beacon/chart disagreement.
anchors.target_state: Deniz has documented multiple independent discrepancies that cannot be dismissed as isolated error.

anchors.title: The Beacon Ridge Records
anchors.purpose: Gather corroborating evidence through the signal-tower network and its keepers.
anchors.target_state: Deniz gains access to historical beacon logs and builds credibility with tower crews.

anchors.title: The Drowned Causeway Passage
anchors.purpose: Gather corroborating evidence through the rare-tide causeway and its physical clues.
anchors.target_state: Deniz recovers physical evidence at the causeway that hints at the markers' unusual age.

anchors.title: Reaching the Tide Observatory
anchors.purpose: Gain entry to the abandoned observatory using whichever evidence route(s) Deniz has pursued.
anchors.target_state: Deniz secures access to the observatory and its instruments, gaining tools to interpret the deeper pattern.

anchors.title: Confronting the True Cause
anchors.purpose: Bring the gathered evidence to a point where the underlying cause of the disagreement must be faced.
anchors.target_state: Deniz has assembled enough verified evidence that the world's institutions must respond to the phenomenon, whatever the character decides to do with it.

anchor_edges.rationale: Initial discrepancies motivate seeking tower records.
From the common branch point, Deniz may pursue the Drowned Causeway instead of Beacon Ridge; neither route requires the other.
Beacon records can unlock observatory access on their own.
Causeway evidence can unlock observatory access on its own.
Evidence from both routes together strengthens the case for entry.
Evidence from both routes together strengthens the case for entry.
Observatory instruments are necessary to interpret and confront the underlying cause.

hidden_truths.question: Who or what built the ancient navigation markers, and why do they no longer align with official charts?
What specific rule-bound tidal/magnetic process is causing the markers to drift out of agreement with charts?
hidden_truths.hidden_statement: The markers are keyed to a slow migration of magnetic stone deposits beneath the deep channels, a natural but rarely observed geophysical cycle.

hidden_truths.question: What did Deniz's father actually record before he disappeared?
hidden_truths.hidden_statement: He documented early signs of the same marker drift years before anyone else noticed, but his report was lost in transit rather than deliberately suppressed.

reveal_intents.summary: Early hints that the drift follows a rhythm rather than random error.
Physical evidence suggests the markers predate every known culture, without confirming who made them.
Observatory instruments confirm the magnetic-stone migration cycle as the true cause.
A fragment of the father's lost survey notes surfaces, hinting he noticed the drift first.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's father disappeared on an expedition years ago, and clues about his fate may surface anywhere in the outer islands.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Gives emotional depth without forcing the Main Saga into a rescue plot.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's mentor holds high evidentiary standards and unexplained gaps in old archive access.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Explores whether trust must be earned mutually, without pre-deciding betrayal.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Merchant captains and island councils disagree over which outer charts to trust, creating economic and political friction.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Shows the world's stakes extend beyond Deniz's personal curiosity.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.

proposed_bindings.description: Beacon Ridge signal towers as evidence-gathering site.
placement_constraints: must remain consistent with established inner-strait geography

proposed_bindings.description: The Drowned Causeway as a rare-tide evidence site.
placement_constraints: only accessible during defined rare tide windows

proposed_bindings.description: The abandoned tide observatory as the convergence point.

integration_rules: Reuse established world locations before inventing new ones.
New NPCs tied to beacon/causeway routes should be reusable in future Episodes.
Keep father's fate and marker origin consistent with hidden truth definitions.

milestones.summary: Deniz notices a beacon reading that disagrees with the official chart by a margin too large for instrument error.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz has one documented anomaly and a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.
consequence_options: The mentor questions Deniz's methodology.
The friend becomes curious and offers to help verify.

milestones.summary: A second, unrelated beacon/chart mismatch surfaces from a different source, suggesting a pattern rather than a fluke.
milestones.state_condition: Two independent discrepancies are documented with different origins, strengthening the case for a real phenomenon.
consequence_options: Harbor crews begin treating Deniz's notes as worth reading.
A merchant captain dismisses the pattern as coincidence, creating friction.

milestones.summary: A third case, cross-checked against archive records, confirms the discrepancies share a rhythm rather than random error.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz possesses three cross-referenced anomalies that cannot be waved away as isolated mistakes, opening the choice of which route to pursue further.
consequence_options: The mentor grants provisional trust for independent fieldwork.
Word spreads and the merchant council begins to take notice.

milestones.summary: Deniz makes a genuine connection with a beacon-tower keeper willing to share informal knowledge.
milestones.state_condition: A tower keeper now regards Deniz as trustworthy enough to speak candidly about irregularities.
consequence_options: The keeper becomes a recurring ally.
Other keepers grow suspicious of the keeper's openness.

milestones.summary: Deniz gains limited access to the tower network's historical log archive.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz can review decades of beacon logs, though some records remain restricted or missing.
consequence_options: Gaps in the archive raise new questions about who removed records.
The mentor learns of the access and reacts with mixed pride and concern.

milestones.summary: Cross-referencing the logs reveals a decades-long drift pattern matching Deniz's own observations, and a fragment referencing a past surveyor's report surfaces.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz has strong documentary evidence of long-term drift, plus a lead pointing toward a previously unverified survey report.
consequence_options: Deniz feels the pull of the search_for_father thread activating.
The mentor trust arc becomes discoverable through unexplained archive gaps.

milestones.summary: Deniz learns to predict the rare tide window that exposes the Drowned Causeway.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz has a reliable method for timing access to the causeway, a resource no casual visitor has.
consequence_options: Local fishers start relying on Deniz's tide predictions.
A rival surveyor tries to beat Deniz to the causeway.

milestones.summary: Deniz secures safe passage onto the exposed causeway during the tide window.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz can physically reach and examine the ancient markers on the causeway.
consequence_options: The friend insists on joining, creating shared risk and reward.
Harbor authorities question the safety of the unsupervised trip.

milestones.summary: Physical inspection of the causeway markers reveals construction and wear patterns inconsistent with any known chart-making era.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz holds physical evidence that the markers are far older than official history accounts for.
consequence_options: Academic circles dismiss the finding without observatory-grade instruments to confirm it.
A merchant faction grows anxious about what unregulated old markers imply for trade routes.

milestones.summary: Deniz compiles the evidence gathered from whichever route(s) were pursued into a coherent case for needing observatory instruments.
milestones.state_condition: A structured, presentable body of evidence exists, sufficient to justify requesting entry to the restricted observatory.
consequence_options: The mentor either sponsors the request or raises objections.
A council official takes interest, for good or self-serving reasons.

milestones.summary: Through sponsorship, negotiation, or demonstrated competence, Deniz obtains formal access to the abandoned tide observatory.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz possesses a legitimate, if provisional, right to use the observatory's instruments.
consequence_options: Access comes with oversight conditions Deniz must respect or risk losing it.
Rival interests attempt to piggyback on the access.

milestones.summary: Whatever combination of beacon and causeway evidence Deniz carries is tested against the observatory's precise instruments, sharpening the picture of the phenomenon.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz has instrument-grade readings that align with prior field evidence, setting up direct confrontation with the underlying cause.
consequence_options: The readings suggest the phenomenon is accelerating, raising urgency.
Instrument logs reveal someone accessed the observatory recently and left it disturbed.

milestones.summary: Instrument analysis confirms the drift is caused by a slow migration of magnetic stone deposits beneath the deep channels.
milestones.state_condition: The natural, rule-bound cause of the discrepancies is verified beyond reasonable doubt, though the markers' origin remains unresolved.
consequence_options: The mentor's old withheld records finally make sense in this new light.
The merchant_chart_dispute side saga intensifies as the finding becomes public knowledge.

milestones.summary: With verified evidence in hand, Deniz reaches a point where multiple credible paths exist for how to act on the discovery.
milestones.state_condition: Institutions, the mentor, and harbor authorities are aware evidence exists and await Deniz's choice of how to present or use it; no path is predetermined.
consequence_options: Publishing openly could reshape trust in official charts but expose Deniz to scrutiny.
Sharing quietly with the mentor first could preserve relationships but slow wider impact.
Alerting merchant councils directly could affect trade routes immediately.

milestones.summary: Whatever path Deniz chooses, the wider world begins visibly reacting to the confirmed phenomenon, changing Deniz's standing and future options.
milestones.state_condition: Deniz's reputation, relationships, and access to future outer-route work shift based on how the discovery was handled, while the marker origin mystery remains open for future sagas.
consequence_options: Deniz gains formal standing to chart beyond the home strait.
Some institutions resist the finding, creating ongoing friction.
The father's lost survey gains renewed interest, opening doors to the search_for_father saga.

hidden_truths.hidden_statement: He documented early signs of the same marker drift years before anyone else noticed, but his report was lost in transit rather than deliberately suppressed.

reveal_steps.summary: Early hints that the drift follows a rhythm rather than random error.
Physical evidence suggests the markers predate every known culture, without confirming who made them.
Observatory instruments confirm the magnetic-stone migration cycle as the true cause.
A fragment of the father's lost survey notes surfaces, hinting he noticed the drift first.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's father disappeared on an expedition years ago, and clues about his fate may surface anywhere in the outer islands.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Gives emotional depth without forcing the Main Saga into a rescue plot.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's mentor holds high evidentiary standards and unexplained gaps in old archive access.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Explores whether trust must be earned mutually, without pre-deciding betrayal.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

latent_side_sagas.premise: Merchant captains and island councils disagree over which outer charts to trust, creating economic and political friction.
latent_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Shows the world's stakes extend beyond Deniz's personal curiosity.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.
